*   Note: $v'[0]$ and $v'[1]$ correspond to the clip-space x and y coordinates, normalized to $[-1, 1]$ before mapping to the viewport [S1].

The claim states that $v'[0]$ and $v'[1]$ correspond to clip-space x and y coordinates normalized to $[-1, 1]$. The evidence in Source [S1] provides the formulas for window coordinates: $wx = V[0] + V[2] · (v'[0] + 1)/2$ and $wy = V[1] + V[3] · (v'[1] + 1)/2$. These formulas are the standard OpenGL viewport transformation equations, which map normalized device coordinates (clip space coordinates) from the range $[-1, 1]$ to window coordinates. Specifically, the term $(v'[i] + 1)/2$ performs the linear mapping from $[-1, 1]$ to $[0, 1]$, which is then scaled by the viewport width/height ($V[2], V[3]$) and offset by the viewport origin ($V[0], V[1]$). Therefore, the evidence supports the claim that $v'[0]$ and $v'[1]$ are the normalized clip-space coordinates.
